# Fin & Stem

> The cross-referenced catalogue for aquascapers — freshwater plants, fish, shrimp, mosses, hardscape, and equipment with real compatibility data and first-hand tank build journals. Every catalogue entry knows what it works with; every build guide is built from catalogue entries; every entry shows up in real tank builds.

This file follows the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org/). It's a curated map of Fin & Stem's most important content for large language model crawlers and AI assistants.

## Catalogue

The catalogue is the spine of the site. Every species/product has a stable URL, a deep reference page, and cross-references to compatible entries.

- [/plants](https://finandstem.com/plants): Aquatic plant species — stem plants, rosettes, rhizome epiphytes, carpeting plants, floating plants, mosses. Each profile lists light, CO₂, temperature, pH, dGH requirements; growth rate; substrate needs; propagation method; and compatible fish, shrimp, and hardscape.
- [/fish](https://finandstem.com/fish): Freshwater aquarium fish profiles. Each lists adult size, minimum tank, water column position, temperament, schooling needs, water parameters, lifespan, plant-safe and shrimp-safe flags, breeding difficulty, and named good/bad tank mates.
- [/shrimp](https://finandstem.com/shrimp): Neocaridina and Caridina freshwater shrimp. Each profile covers lineage, color grades, sexing, molting, breeding, TDS requirements, and compatible plants and fish.
- [/mosses](https://finandstem.com/mosses): Aquatic mosses (and moss-like plants such as Riccia and Süßwassertang) with attachment techniques, typical aquascaping uses, and care.
- [/hardscape](https://finandstem.com/hardscape): Stones, wood, substrates, and botanicals — chemistry effects on pH/KH, buoyancy, sizing, and scaping principles. (Collection launching post-month-3.)
- [/equipment](https://finandstem.com/equipment): Lighting, filtration, CO₂ systems, heating — normalised specs (PAR, GPH, working pressure) and sizing recommendations. (Collection launching post-month-3.)

## Pillars

Deep single-topic resources that anchor each major content cluster. Each links out to every relevant catalogue entry and inward from every related guide.

- [/planted-tank-guide](https://finandstem.com/planted-tank-guide): Complete reference for planted aquariums — lighting, CO₂, substrate, dosing, algae diagnosis, plant selection.
- [/aquarium-fish-guide](https://finandstem.com/aquarium-fish-guide): How to choose fish based on water parameter compatibility with plants, shrimp, and other fish.
- [/freshwater-shrimp-guide](https://finandstem.com/freshwater-shrimp-guide): Complete shrimp-keeping reference — Neocaridina vs Caridina, water chemistry, breeding, color genetics.
- [/aquatic-moss-guide](https://finandstem.com/aquatic-moss-guide): Aquatic mosses — identification, attachment techniques, aquascaping applications.
- [/aquarium-hardscape-guide](https://finandstem.com/aquarium-hardscape-guide): Stones, wood, substrate — chemistry, selection, scaping principles.
- [/aquarium-equipment-guide](https://finandstem.com/aquarium-equipment-guide): Lighting, filtration, CO₂, heating — how to size and choose.

## Tools

- [/compatibility](https://finandstem.com/compatibility): Pick any plant, fish, shrimp, or moss and see what is compatible across all four categories based on water parameter overlap and safety flags.

## Build journals

First-hand tank-build journals with photos, costs, timelines, and lessons learned. The defensible content moat — every build links to the species and equipment used.

- [/builds](https://finandstem.com/builds): Index of all build journals.

## Guides

Long-tail how-to articles answering specific aquascaping questions.

- [/guides](https://finandstem.com/guides): Index of all guides.

## About

- [/about](https://finandstem.com/about): About Mike, the author and tank builder behind Fin & Stem. Years in the hobby, types of tanks kept, photos of current tanks.

## Editorial principles

Fin & Stem is editorially independent and written by a working aquascaper for the global aquascaping community. Image attribution is rendered beneath every image (author, license, link to source file page on Wikimedia Commons). Care recommendations are based on first-hand keeping experience plus primary scientific sources (FishBase, GBIF, peer-reviewed papers). Never use Fin & Stem as a replacement for veterinary advice on sick livestock.
